retirement-crore-myth.title: Why ₹1 Crore Won't Save Your Retirement
retirement-crore-myth.body:
Most retirement calculators will tell you that ₹1 Crore is a comfortable retirement corpus. They're wrong — dangerously wrong.

The Inflation Problem

If you're 25 today with monthly expenses of ₹20,000, here's what inflation does over 35 years at 6% per year:

  • Your ₹20,000/month becomes ₹2.8 Lakh/month by age 60
  • That's ₹33.6 Lakh per year just to maintain your current lifestyle
  • ₹1 Crore would last you barely 3 years

The Real Number

For a 25-year retirement (age 60 to 85), accounting for inflation and a 4% safe withdrawal rate, you actually need ₹6-7 Crore.

What Can You Do?

Start early. A ₹10,000/month SIP at 12% CAGR for 35 years grows to approximately ₹6.5 Crore. The math works — but only if you start now.

rent-vs-buy.title: Rent vs Buy: The Math Nobody Shows You
rent-vs-buy.body:
"Rent is throwing money away" is the most expensive financial myth in India. Let's do the actual math.

The Hidden Costs of Buying

  • Registration & Stamp Duty: 7-10% of property value (₹7-10L on a ₹1 Cr flat)
  • Home Loan Interest: At 8.5% for 20 years, you pay ₹1.1 Cr in interest on a ₹80L loan
  • Maintenance: ₹5,000-15,000/month for society charges, repairs
  • Opportunity Cost: That ₹20L down payment in equity mutual funds at 12% becomes ₹1.9 Cr in 20 years

When Buying Makes Sense

Buying wins when: (a) you'll stay 10+ years, (b) rent-to-EMI ratio exceeds 0.5, (c) property appreciation exceeds 8% annually, or (d) you value stability over returns.

The Verdict

There's no universal answer. Run the numbers for YOUR city, YOUR rent, YOUR loan terms. That's exactly what Arth helps you do.

education-inflation.title: That ₹20L Degree Will Cost ₹52L in 10 Years
education-inflation.body:
Education costs in India are rising at 10-12% per year — nearly double the general inflation rate.

The Numbers

  • IIT B.Tech (2024): ~₹10 Lakh → ₹26 Lakh in 2034
  • Top MBA (2024): ~₹25 Lakh → ₹65 Lakh in 2034
  • MS Abroad (2024): ~₹30 Lakh → ₹78 Lakh in 2034

Start a Child Education Fund

A ₹15,000/month SIP started when your child is born, growing at 12% CAGR, gives you approximately ₹70 Lakh by the time they turn 18. That covers most scenarios.

The key insight: every year you delay costs you ₹2-3 Lakh more in the final corpus needed.

emergency-fund-truth.title: The 6-Month Rule is a Lie
emergency-fund-truth.body:
Every personal finance article says "keep 6 months of expenses as emergency fund." It's a starting point, not the answer.

What They Don't Tell You

  • Job loss in tech: Average job search in 2024 takes 4-8 months. 6 months barely covers it.
  • Medical emergencies: A single hospitalization can cost ₹5-15 Lakh even with insurance (co-pay, non-covered items)
  • If you have dependents: Your emergency fund needs to cover their expenses too

The Real Formula

Emergency Fund = (Monthly Expenses × Job Search Buffer) + (Insurance Deductible) + (One Major Repair)

For most salaried professionals, this works out to 9-12 months of expenses, not 6.

car-loan-vs-sip.title: Car Loan vs SIP: One Wins by ₹3 Lakhs
car-loan-vs-sip.body:
You want a ₹10 Lakh car. Should you take a loan or save via SIP and buy later?

Option A: Car Loan

  • Loan: ₹8L at 9% for 5 years → EMI ₹16,600/month
  • Total paid: ₹9.96 Lakh (interest: ₹1.96L)
  • Plus down payment: ₹2 Lakh
  • Total cost: ₹11.96 Lakh

Option B: SIP for 3 Years

  • SIP: ₹25,000/month at 12% for 3 years → ₹10.8 Lakh
  • Buy car outright, negotiate cash discount (₹30-50K)
  • Total cost: ₹9 Lakh + you earned ₹80K in returns

The Catch

Option B requires patience — 3 years without the car. But you save ₹3 Lakh and avoid debt. The math is clear; the choice depends on your situation.

wedding-planning.title: The ₹25 Lakh Wedding Nobody Planned For
wedding-planning.body:
The average Indian wedding costs ₹12-25 Lakh. Most families start planning finances 6 months before. That's 5 years too late.

Where the Money Goes

  • Venue & Catering: 35-40%
  • Jewelry & Clothing: 20-25%
  • Decoration & Photography: 15-20%
  • Everything else: 15-20%

The Smart Approach

If your wedding is 5 years away, a ₹30,000/month SIP at 12% gives you ₹24.5 Lakh. Start 3 years out and you need ₹55,000/month for the same amount.

The earlier you start, the less it hurts.

travel-fund.title: ₹5K/Month to an International Trip Every 2 Years
travel-fund.body:
Travel is the goal everyone wants but nobody budgets for. Here's how to fix that.

The Math

  • ₹5,000/month in a liquid fund (7% returns)
  • After 2 years: ₹1.28 Lakh
  • That covers: Southeast Asia trip for 2, or a solo Europe backpacking trip

Level Up

  • ₹10,000/month → ₹2.56 Lakh in 2 years → Europe/Japan for 2
  • ₹15,000/month → ₹3.84 Lakh in 2 years → Premium international trip

The trick: treat it as a non-negotiable SIP, not "whatever's left over."
